sections.heading: What Causes Foggy Windows and Why You Should Act Now
sections.body: Foggy windows are caused by seal failure in insulated glass units (IGUs). Over time, temperature fluctuations, UV exposure, and normal wear cause the edge seals on double- or triple-pane windows to break down. Once the seal is compromised, the inert gas — typically argon or krypton — that provides insulation escapes, and humid outdoor air rushes in. That moisture condenses on the inner glass surfaces, creating the cloudy, streaky appearance that no amount of cleaning can fix. Left unaddressed, broken foggy windows reduce your home's R-value, drive up heating and cooling costs, and can lead to mold growth around the window frame. For Arlington residents dealing with the region's hot, humid summers and cold winters, a broken seal means your HVAC system is working overtime. faq.q: What exactly is a foggy window and can it be repaired without replacing the whole window?
faq.a: A foggy window occurs when the hermetic seal on a double- or triple-pane insulated glass unit fails, allowing moisture to enter the space between the panes. The result is a cloudy or hazy appearance that cannot be cleaned from the outside. In most cases, yes — you do not need to replace the entire window. Our technicians can remove and replace only the insulated glass unit while keeping your existing frame, saving you significant money. faq.q: Will repairing my foggy windows actually improve my energy bills?
faq.a: Yes, significantly. When the seal on an insulated glass unit fails, the insulating gas escapes and is replaced by ordinary air or moisture. This dramatically reduces the window's thermal resistance, or R-value, meaning your heating and cooling system must work harder to maintain comfortable indoor temperatures. Replacing the failed IGU restores the window's original insulating performance. Arlington homeowners and property managers routinely report noticeable reductions in energy costs after broken foggy window repair. Many modern replacement IGUs also include low-E coatings that further reduce solar heat gain, improving efficiency beyond the original installation.

faq.q: How do I know if my window seal is broken or if there is another problem?
faq.a: The most common sign of a broken window seal is persistent fogging, cloudiness, or streaking between the panes that does not go away and cannot be wiped clean. You may also notice condensation that appears in the morning and dissipates by afternoon, or a visible film or mineral deposits on the inner glass surfaces. In some cases, the window frame may also show signs of moisture damage. If you are unsure, our technicians will perform a free on-site inspection to confirm seal failure and rule out other issues such as frame damage or improper installation.
